install_notes: py -3.12 -m venv .venv; pip install pystac-client planetary-computer odc-stac numpy rasterio dask psutil truststore: all wheels, clean on py3.12.10 Windows 11
problems: Load took 792.8 s for 546 items x 7 bands (~3,800 COG window reads); 13x over the 60 s bar.
Per-read latency is several seconds: a 30-item single-band test took 4.7 s with 32 threads, so throughput is limited by HTTPS round trips, not CPU or bytes.

This machine's Norton Antivirus intercepts TLS (re-signs certs). certifi-based Python failed with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED; fixed with truststore + exporting the Windows root store as CURL_CA_BUNDLE for GDAL. Norton scanning probably inflates per-request latency too, so these timings are likely worse than a clean network.
Only one full run done (deadline). Not tried: 64-128 threads on the full set, GDAL_HTTP_MULTIPLEX/HTTP2, or loading only the needed months per chapter.
notes: Search: one CQL2 query (OR of 43 June-Sept windows, eo:cloud_cover<50), 8.7 s, 546 items (L4 7, L5, L7, L8, L9). odc.stac.load(bbox, crs=EPSG:32611, resolution=30, groupby=solar_day, chunks 2048) -> 544 time slices of 206x207 px, all 7 bands, dask threads=32, fail_on_error=False. Data is real: median red reflectance by year is in median_red_reflectance_by_year (0.04-0.21, trending upward over time; plausible for a shrinking lake but not verified). All 43 years 1984-2026 have data. Verdict: odc-stac works and is correct, but reading every summer scene is far too slow here; fetch fewer scenes (e.g. best 1-3 per year) or use server-side composites.
